title: Ensemble pressure test standup notes - Nov 22 2026
content:
Purpose:
Weekly standup notes for the ensemble pressure test experiment (mixed-model routing + quantized fallback). Capture observed regressions, quick triage, and next steps.

Context / setup:
- Goal: run 2h pressure window to reproduce a customer-like ensemble: router -> primary model (fp16-8b) with fallback to q4_0-8b when capacity constrained. Include KV prefill and prefix cache enabled.
- Traffic profile: steady-state 5% shadowed production RPS (~1.2k total shadow qps), 30% chat-style sequences (>512 tokens), 70% short (<=128).
- Test harness: bench-driver v0.9.8 with profile "ensemble-compat-1024". Warmup 15m, pressure 90m, cooldown 15m.
- Key metrics: overall throughput (qps), p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), model-switch rate (% of requests falling back), KV cache hit ratio, GPU util per-instance.

Run summary (Nov 22 09:00 - 12:00 PT)
- Baseline run (no routing changes) matched prior baseline: 1.2k qps steady, p99 ~108ms, KV cache hit ratio 0.72.
- Ensemble run (routing + fallback): initial 30m stable, then two distinct degradation windows at +35m and +76m.
  - Degradation #1 (+35m): throughput dropped from 1.1k -> 680 qps; p99 spiked 108ms -> 420ms; model-switch rate jumped 4% -> 28% in 10m. KV cache hit ratio decreased 0.72 -> 0.48.
  - Degradation #2 (+76m): throughput partially recovered to ~860 qps, then second spike where p99 hit 610ms for ~6 minutes; GPU memory pressure on node pool b increased and OOM throttles observed on 2 pods.
- Observed difference vs earlier microbench sessions: higher tail when the router switched >15% requests to q4_0 under warm GPU reuse conditions. Not a pure q4 throughput limit — appears to be an interaction between model-switching, KV eviction, and kernel heat-up.

Initial hypotheses:
1) KV cache eviction cascade: the sudden increase in model-switch leads to cache keyspace fragmentation (different model variants maintain separate cache keys) causing more misses and extra KV loads which amplify per-request work.
2) Kernel warm-up mismatch: switching between fp16 and q4 kernels causes heat-up of different CUDA kernels and temporary scheduling contention, increasing latency spikes.
3) Autoscaler hysteresis: autoscaler didn't spin up compatible q4 instances fast enough, causing bursts of requests queued on limited GPUs and transient OOMs.
4) Memory and CUDA streams: when model variant switch occurs frequently, per-request stream creation and cross-stream synchronization penalties accumulate.

Data captured / artifacts:
- Perf traces: perf-trace-2026-11-22/ensemble-run-09h35.pcap.gz (attached to RINF-8421)
- Logs: router logs (router-prod-shadow-11-22.log), model-serving logs (model-b-q4.log), pod metrics snapshots (nodepool-b-09h40-metrics.json).
- Bench commands used:
  - ./bench-driver --profile ensemble-compat-1024 --duration 7200 --warmup 900 --shadow 0.05 --outdir /tmp/bench/nov22
  - kubectl top pods -n serving --selector=pool=nodepool-b --containers

Quick triage notes from meeting:
- Diego: looked at router metrics; saw routing thrash at the two degradation timestamps. Router reported a burst of health-check-based reassigns when q4 pool experienced short GC pauses. Linked to PR #2375 which changed q4 eviction behavior.
- Priya: KV traces show increased miss-rate correlated to model switch windows. Confirmed cache key namespace currently includes model-variant as part of the key (intended) — this increases working set when many variants are served.
- Samir: GPU-side telemetry shows stream stall patterns and increased cudaMemcpy syncs in the first degradation window. These line up with kernel warm-up hypothesis.
- Eleni: Autoscaler logs indicate scale-up attempts but minimum cooldown prevented further pod creation until after the worst of the spike; policy tuned for stable workloads, not rapid ensemble switchover.

Immediate action items (owners + ETA):
1) Short-term configuration change: disable model-variant-splitting of KV keys for the ensemble shadow (single shared prefix) to test if hit ratio stabilizes. Owner: Priya. ETA: 11/23 EOD.
2) Kernel warm-up experiment: add background warmers that pre-invoke q4 kernels on spare GPUs to reduce first-use penalties. Owner: Samir. Run test 11/24 morning.
3) Autoscaler tweak: temporarily lower scale-down cooldown and enable burst-scaling for the shadow pool to validate autoscaler hysteresis impact. Owner: Eleni. ETA: 11/24 mid-day.
4) Instrumentation: add a lightweight per-request tag that logs whether a request experienced model-switch and whether it hit KV cache; aggregate via metrics pipeline. Owner: Diego. ETA: 11/25.
5) Follow-up postmortem doc: collect all traces and write a short retro with confirmed root cause(s) and recommended defaults for ensemble routing. Owner: Asha. ETA: 11/29.

Longer-term experiments / ideas:
- Evaluate a unified cache layer that is variant-agnostic but stores entries with variant-translation metadata to avoid duplication of keyspace.
- Explore kernel-agnostic request queueing: batch requests by target kernel to reduce warm-up churn at cost of small latency tradeoff.
- Model routing soft-thresholds: ramp fallback rate slowly when capacity is near threshold to avoid thundering model-switch cascades.

Open questions to resolve in next sync:
- If KV key unification fixes hit ratio regressions, does model correctness/response variance remain acceptable? (Priya to validate on sample prompts)
- Can we reproduce the exact OOM signature in a smaller dev cluster for deeper profiler attachment? (Samir)
- Should we add canonical ensemble test to CI with small scale to prevent regressions from PRs like #2375? (Diego)

Next sync:
- Quick async updates in the bench channel by EOD 11/24. Follow-up in-person sync Fri 11/26 10:30 PT to review experiment results.

Meeting attendees: Asha Mehta, Diego Alvarez, Priya Kapoor, Samir Reddy, Eleni Papadopoulos, Jordan Liu (observability).

Notes to self:
- Keep bench seed consistent between runs (set --rand-seed) to make diffs reproducible.
- Capture pod-level cuda stats at 1s granularity during next run.
summary: Standup notes for an ensemble pressure test that revealed two latency/regression windows likely caused by KV cache fragmentation and kernel warm-up during model switching. Immediate actions assigned to reduce cache fragmentation, warm kernels, and adjust autoscaler settings; follow-up retro scheduled.
